probabilityNote: Probability is an estimate of how likely a question is, based on common patterns in PCI-syllabus pharmacy papers. It is not a promise.

questions.question: State Hückel's rule and apply it to three compounds.
questions.answer: Cyclic, planar, fully conjugated with (4n+2) π e−. Benzene 6 (aromatic), cyclobutadiene 4 (antiaromatic), cyclopentadienyl anion 6 (aromatic).

questions.question: Give the limitations of Friedel–Crafts alkylation.
questions.answer: Polyalkylation, carbocation rearrangement (n-propyl → cumene), fails on deactivated rings and –NH2 rings, aryl/vinyl halides don't react, reversible.

questions.question: Write the mechanism of nitration of benzene.
questions.answer: HNO3 + 2H2SO4 → NO2+; ring attacks NO2+ → σ-complex; HSO4− removes H+ → nitrobenzene.

questions.question: Explain the orbital structure of benzene.
questions.answer: sp2 carbons, 120°, planar; six p orbitals overlap → π clouds above and below; delocalised 6 e−.

questions.question: Synthesis and uses of saccharin.
questions.answer: Toluene → ClSO3H → NH3 → KMnO4 → heat (–H2O). Sweetener 300–500× sugar for diabetics.

questions.question: Why are halogens deactivating but o/p directing?
questions.answer: –I lowers ring electron density (slower); lone pairs (+R) stabilise o/p σ-complex.

questions.question: Prove benzene's extra stability (resonance energy).
questions.answer: Expected ΔH hydrogenation 85.8, found 49.8 kcal/mol → 36 kcal/mol resonance energy.

questions.question: Structure and uses of DDT and BHC.
questions.answer: DDT: chlorobenzene + chloral (H2SO4), insecticide. BHC: benzene + 3Cl2 in UV, γ-isomer lindane for scabies/lice.

questions.question: Write a note on chloramine-T.
questions.answer: Sodium N-chloro-p-toluenesulfonamide; from p-toluenesulfonamide + NaOCl; releases active Cl; antiseptic, disinfectant.

questions.question: Sulfonation is reversible — explain with use.
questions.answer: SO3 electrophile; dilute acid/steam removes –SO3H; used as a blocking group.

questions.question: Why is cyclooctatetraene non-aromatic?
questions.answer: Tub-shaped (not planar), 8 π e− (4n); behaves like an alkene.

questions.question: Explain the effect of substituents on reactivity and orientation in EAS, with examples.
questions.answer: Define I and R effects; classify groups (see the notes); draw σ-complex resonance for anisole (o/p) and nitrobenzene (meta); halogen exception; toluene hyperconjugation.

questions.question: Describe the structure of benzene: Kekulé, resonance and orbital picture, with evidence.
questions.answer: Kekulé + 4 objections; bond length 1.39 Å; resonance hybrid; sp2 orbital diagram; resonance energy calculation; aromaticity rules.

questions.question: Give the general EAS mechanism and explain nitration, sulfonation, halogenation and Friedel–Crafts reactions.
questions.answer: 3-step mechanism + energy diagram; electrophile generation and equation for each; FC limitations; acylation advantages.

questions.question: Write the synthesis, structure and uses of DDT, saccharin, BHC and chloramine-T.
questions.answer: One labelled equation and 2–3 uses each; mention bans/toxicity for DDT and BHC.

questions.question: Explain the acidity of phenol and the effect of substituents.
questions.answer: Phenoxide resonance-stabilised; EWG (–NO2) increase, EDG (–CH3) decrease acidity; picric > p-nitro > m-nitro > phenol > cresol.

questions.question: Why is aniline a weaker base than ammonia?
questions.answer: N lone pair delocalised into ring; anilinium loses this resonance; sp2 carbon –I.

questions.question: Write any four synthetic uses of benzenediazonium chloride.
questions.answer: Sandmeyer (CuCl → ArCl, CuCN → ArCN), KI → ArI, H2O → phenol, H3PO2 → benzene, coupling → azo dyes.

questions.question: Give qualitative tests for phenol.
questions.answer: FeCl3 violet; Br2 water white ppt; Liebermann nitroso green→red→blue; phthalein pink.

questions.question: Structure and uses of cresol, resorcinol and naphthols.
questions.answer: Cresol = methylphenol, disinfectant (Lysol); resorcinol = 1,3-diOH, keratolytic; α/β-naphthol: Molisch test, azo dyes.

questions.question: What is diazotisation? Why is it done at 0–5 °C?
questions.answer: ArNH2 + NaNO2/HCl → ArN2+Cl−; above 5 °C it loses N2 to phenol.

questions.question: Compare acidity of benzoic acid, phenol and acetic acid.
questions.answer: Benzoic (4.2) > acetic (4.76) > phenol (10); two equivalent O in carboxylate; phenyl –I.

questions.question: Explain the ortho effect.
questions.answer: Ortho group twists COOH out of plane → benzoic acids stronger; crowds NH3+ → anilines weaker.

questions.question: Kolbe–Schmidt and Reimer–Tiemann reactions.
questions.answer: Phenoxide + CO2 → salicylic acid; phenol + CHCl3/NaOH → salicylaldehyde via :CCl2.

questions.question: Why does phenol not react with NaHCO3?
questions.answer: Phenol (pKa 10) is weaker than H2CO3 (6.4), so cannot release CO2.

questions.question: Discuss the preparation of diazonium salts and their synthetic applications.
questions.answer: Diazotisation equation + mechanism; stability at 0–5 °C; full diazonium wheel with named reactions; coupling conditions; drug links (prontosil, Bratton–Marshall).

questions.question: Explain acidity of phenols and basicity of aromatic amines with effect of substituents.
questions.answer: Phenoxide and aniline resonance; pKa/pKb tables; o/m/p nitro comparison; H-bond in o-nitrophenol; ortho effect.

questions.question: Describe the acidity of benzoic acid, effect of substituents, and its reactions and uses.
questions.answer: Benzoate resonance; substituent pKa table; ortho effect; reaction table; FeCl3 test; preservative uses.

questions.question: Write structure, tests and uses of phenol, cresols, resorcinol and naphthols.
questions.answer: Structures; tests table; uses table with pharmacy examples.

questions.question: Define iodine value; give its principle, method and significance.
questions.answer: g I2 absorbed per 100 g fat; halogen adds to C=C; Wijs ICl, KI, thiosulfate titration; measures unsaturation, classifies drying oils.

questions.question: Define saponification value and give its significance.
questions.answer: mg KOH to saponify 1 g fat; reflux with alcoholic KOH, back-titrate with HCl; inversely related to molecular weight; detects adulteration.

questions.question: What is rancidity? Give its types and prevention.
questions.answer: Bad smell/taste on storage; hydrolytic, oxidative, ketonic; prevent with cool dark airtight storage and antioxidants (BHA, BHT, vitamin E).

questions.question: Define acid value and give its significance.
questions.answer: mg KOH to neutralise free FA in 1 g; titrate in ethanol–ether with KOH; high value = rancid/poor quality.

questions.question: Write a note on Reichert–Meissl value.
questions.answer: mL 0.1 N alkali for steam-volatile water-soluble FA from 5 g; high in butter (17–35); detects ghee adulteration.

questions.question: Explain hydrogenation of oils with its importance.
questions.answer: H2 + Ni at 180 °C adds to C=C; oil → solid fat (vanaspati); lowers IV, improves keeping; trans fats concern.

questions.question: Explain saponification with equation.
questions.answer: Triglyceride + 3 NaOH → glycerol + 3 soap; Na soap hard, K soap soft.

questions.question: Define acetyl value and ester value.
questions.answer: Acetyl: mg KOH for acetic acid from 1 g acetylated fat → free –OH (castor high). Ester = SV − AV.

questions.question: Classify fatty acids with examples.
questions.answer: Saturated (palmitic, stearic), unsaturated (oleic, linoleic, linolenic), hydroxy (ricinoleic); essential FA.

questions.question: Define and explain the principle, method and significance of acid value, saponification value, iodine value and RM value.
questions.answer: Four structured blocks (definition → principle → method → formula → meaning) + typical values table.

questions.question: Discuss the chemical reactions of fats and oils: hydrolysis, hydrogenation, saponification and rancidity.
questions.answer: Equations for each; rancidity types table + autoxidation steps; antioxidants; pharmaceutical relevance.

questions.question: Write about fatty acids and the analytical constants used to evaluate oils.
questions.answer: Fatty acid table; then all six constants briefly with significance.

questions.question: Write Haworth synthesis of naphthalene.
questions.answer: Benzene + succinic anhydride (AlCl3) → Clemmensen → H2SO4 ring closure → Clemmensen → Se dehydrogenation.

questions.question: Why does naphthalene undergo EAS at the α-position?
questions.answer: α-attack σ-complex has two resonance forms keeping one ring benzenoid; β has one; more stable → faster.

questions.question: Give the synthesis and reactions of anthracene.
questions.answer: Benzene + phthalic anhydride → o-benzoylbenzoic acid → H2SO4 → anthraquinone → Zn dust. Reactions at C9/C10: oxidation, reduction, Br2, Diels–Alder.

questions.question: Synthesis and uses of triphenylmethane.
questions.answer: 3 C6H6 + CHCl3 (AlCl3) or Grignard; trityl ion/radical; dyes (gentian violet, malachite green), clotrimazole.

questions.question: Synthesis and reactions of diphenylmethane.
questions.answer: Benzene + benzyl chloride (AlCl3); oxidation → benzophenone; benzhydryl antihistamines.

questions.question: Write the structure, synthesis and medicinal importance of phenanthrene.
questions.answer: Angular C14H10; Haworth or Pschorr; reactions at 9,10; steroid nucleus and morphine.

questions.question: Explain sulfonation of naphthalene at 80 °C and 160 °C.
questions.answer: Kinetic 1-sulfonic acid at 80 °C; thermodynamic 2-sulfonic acid at 160 °C (no peri strain).

questions.question: Compare anthracene and phenanthrene.
questions.answer: Both C14H10; linear vs angular; phenanthrene more stable (92 vs 84 kcal/mol, 5 vs 4 resonance forms); both react at 9,10.

questions.question: Write Gomberg's free radical.
questions.answer: Trityl chloride + Ag/Zn → (C6H5)3C•, stabilised by resonance over three rings.

questions.question: Discuss structure, synthesis and chemical reactions of naphthalene with medicinal uses.
questions.answer: Numbering diagram, resonance, bond lengths; Haworth synthesis; reactions table with α-preference explanation and sulfonation temperature; drugs list.

questions.question: Write the synthesis and reactions of anthracene and phenanthrene.
questions.answer: Both structures; anthraquinone route and Haworth/Pschorr; 9,10 reactions; medicinal importance (laxatives, anthracyclines, steroids).

questions.question: Describe the synthesis, reactions and uses of diphenylmethane and triphenylmethane.
questions.answer: Friedel–Crafts and Grignard routes; benzylic reactions; trityl cation/anion/radical; dyes and drugs.

questions.question: State Baeyer's strain theory and give its limitations.
questions.answer: Flat rings; d = ½(109°28' − α); cyclopropane most strained. Fails: cyclohexane most stable, large rings stable, rings not flat, ignores torsional strain.

questions.question: Explain Coulson–Moffitt's concept of banana bonds.
questions.answer: Hybrid orbitals can't close below ~104°; overlap outside the internuclear line → bent, weak bonds → easy ring opening; less strain than Baeyer predicted.

questions.question: Draw and compare chair and boat forms of cyclohexane.
questions.answer: Chair: staggered, no strain, most stable. Boat: eclipsed bonds + flagpole H clash, 6.9 kcal/mol higher.

questions.question: Write the Sachse–Mohr theory of strainless rings.
questions.answer: Rings ≥ 6 puckered, keep 109°28'; chair/boat; Mohr predicted cis/trans decalin; Hückel isolated both.

questions.question: Give methods of preparation and reactions of cyclopropane.
questions.answer: Freund (1,3-dibromopropane + Zn), malonic ester, Simmons–Smith; ring-opening with H2, Br2, HBr, H2SO4; no KMnO4 reaction.

questions.question: Explain axial and equatorial bonds; why is methylcyclohexane equatorial?
questions.answer: 6 axial (up/down), 6 equatorial (outward); axial CH3 suffers 1,3-diaxial interactions (~1.7 kcal/mol).

questions.question: Calculate angle strain for cyclopropane and cyclobutane.
Name given cycloalkanes by IUPAC rules.
questions.answer: Prefix cyclo-, lowest locants, alphabetical order, cis/trans.

questions.question: Compare reactivity of cyclopropane and cyclobutane.
questions.answer: Cyclopropane opens with Br2/HBr at room temp; cyclobutane needs heat; due to higher strain in cyclopropane.

questions.question: Discuss Baeyer's strain theory with its limitations, Coulson–Moffitt modification and Sachse–Mohr theory.
questions.answer: Postulates, formula and deviation table; heat-of-combustion evidence; 5 limitations; banana bond diagram; strainless rings, decalin proof.

questions.question: Explain conformational analysis of cyclohexane and its derivatives.
questions.answer: Chair, boat, twist-boat, half-chair with energies; ring flip; axial/equatorial; methylcyclohexane; disubstituted table.

questions.question: Write methods of preparation and chemical reactions of cyclopropane and cyclobutane, explaining their stability.
questions.answer: Freund, malonic ester, Simmons–Smith; reaction comparison table; strain-based explanation.
